author: Laura Zhou
description:
As conflicts around the world highlight the vulnerability of global shipping lanes, China and Russia are reportedly weighing the possibility of turning a vast river into an inland cargo route to the rest of the world.
At the heart of this ambition is the 4,248km (2,640-mile) Irtysh River, which originates in China’s western Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region and runs through Kazakhstan before flowing into Russia’s Ob River and ending in the Arctic Ocean.
To China, this river-to-sea shipping route...
title: Is the Irtysh River the choke-free Arctic shipping gateway that China needs?

author: Chao Kong
description:
A Chinese coastguard ship is shielding a cluster of fishing boats when several small, fast vessels begin circling – sometimes darting closer, sometimes backing off. Are they just curious fishermen? Or are they probing for a weak spot, trying to lure the patrol ship into a trap?
In the real world, a split-second decision could escalate a tense maritime stand-off into something far more dangerous. This is exactly the kind of nerve‑wracking scenario Chinese coastguard researchers have been running...
title: Chinese coastguard has 0.3% chance of using weapons in disputed waters, war game suggests

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin are expected to discuss the Power of Siberia 2 project in a meeting in Bishkek on Monday, according to the Kremlin.
The meeting in Kyrgyzstan’s capital will be their second face-to-face talks this year, following Putin’s trip to Beijing shortly after a visit there by US President Donald Trump.
“The issue will be discussed bilaterally,” Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov was quoted as saying on Friday by Russian news agency...
title: Xi, Putin to meet in Bishkek for Power of Siberia 2 pipeline talks: Kremlin

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Japan plans to deploy fighter jets in India for the first time next month, a decision experts say reflects Tokyo’s desire to strengthen security cooperation with “like-minded” countries in the Indo-Pacific region as it ramps up defence spending in response to China’s growing military power.
According to a Japan Air Self-Defence Force announcement on Tuesday, Tokyo will conduct a joint training exercise, Veer Guardian 26, with the Indian Air Force between September 9 and 21 in Rajasthan in...
title: What Japan’s coming fighter jet deployment to India means for China

author: Laura Zhou,Fan Chen
description:
Gulf states are making a strategic pivot as the war in Iran drags on into its sixth month but observers warned that their shift towards self-reliant defence networks could test China’s “involvement without commitment” strategy in the region.
The war has forced Gulf leaders to face the reality that neither the United States nor China is able to protect them from attacks by Iran.
On Wednesday, the Iranian army warned that any “possible future war” with the US could spread across the region and...
title: China’s Middle East policy at a crossroads 6 months into US-Israeli war on Iran

author: Carol Yang
description:
Video footage taken moments before a catastrophic mudslide hit a border post in Tibet shows how one police officer stationed there tried to guide civilians to safety.
The clip, which shows the officer trying to direct people away from the police station at Gyirong Port, went viral online in China over the weekend.
State broadcaster CCTV said the officer, whom it named as Huang Peng, also rushed into a nearby tourist service centre to tell those inside to evacuate.
The 34-year-old, who had served...
title: China-Nepal floods: police officer filmed guiding people away from stricken border post

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Speak a few sentences of your hometown dialect into a microphone at a museum in central China, and a machine will pinpoint exactly where you are from.
The interactive voice-recognition booth is among star attractions at a new language resources hall that opened on Monday at the Hunan Museum in Changsha.
The hall showcases recordings and other language materials from Chinese dialects, minority languages and oral culture collected over the past decade. The compilation from more than 1,800 field...
title: 10 years, 1,800 survey sites: inside China’s hi-tech push to map linguistic diversity

author: Orange Wang
description:
China is being urged to use human translators to refine AI renderings of its political messaging, amid concern that literal translations can make Beijing’s language sound more threatening abroad.
An article in a state-affiliated academic newspaper said the country should strengthen its translation capacity and guard against AI-generated distortions to improve how its policies and intentions were understood overseas.
As AI takes on more translation work, human translators should work alongside...
title: AI can make China’s political language sound more threatening, scholar warns

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Chinese rescuers continued searching for survivors from this week’s devastating floods along the border with Nepal as the operation passed a critical 72-hour window.
Two villagers near the Gyirong border checkpoint were rescued from the rubble at around 1am on Saturday, according to Tibet’s emergency bureau.
But at the border crossing itself, there was no sign of any survivors. Liu Maolin, the rescue team leader, said the checkpoint building had been completely destroyed by a mudslide.
Seven...
title: China-Nepal floods: rescuers pull 2 survivors out of rubble near Tibet border crossing

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China’s GJ-21 large stealth attack drone has been spotted on flight tests this month, as the country’s first Type 076 amphibious assault ship – the vessel that will launch the drone – enters its final sea trials.
The GJ-21, the naval variant of the GJ-11 stealth attack drone, first appeared at China’s Victory Day parade in September last year and has made rare public appearances since then.
Computer-generated footage aired by state broadcaster CCTV in July showed how it would be launched from...
title: China tests GJ-21 stealth drone as Sichuan Type 076 warship carries out sea trials

author: Alex Lo
description:
In contemporary discourse, the bogeyman of “debt traps” is almost exclusively tied to Beijing. Western media, think tanks, NGOs and policymakers from Washington to Brussels frequently warn developing nations of the perils of bilateral loans from China. Yet, Grenada’s debt dispute from a decade ago and St Vincent and the Grenadines’ (SVG) current troubles offer a starkly different, and often ignored, counter-narrative: the weaponisation of debt by Taiwan.
For years, Grenada has grappled with...
title: Taipei’s debt hardball carries a clear warning for its remaining allies
